basic_identification.full_title: VELOCITY SCALE SET FOR METEOROLOGICAL PURPOSES

scope.summary: This standard covers the general and functional requirements of rigid velocity scale sets used for determining the wind speed from the plotted hodograph of the pilot balloon ascents for meteorological purposes.

requirements.detail: The velocity set scale shall consist of either 3-scales or a square with its four edges suitably graduated. For 3-scale sets, each individual scale is utilized for different portions of the plotted balloon ascent hodograph based on specific scale factors.

The first velocity interval of 10 m/s must be marked such that the 10 m/s mark is positioned on the left and the 0 (zero) m/s mark is on the right. Subsequent graduations are provided at every 5 m/s interval.
Plastic scales must have smooth, even sides and be completely free from blisters, porosity, and structural defects. They must exhibit uniform width and thickness throughout their entire length.
Metal scales must be manufactured completely free from seams, flaws, scales, burrs, and other physical defects, maintaining a uniform thickness and width throughout.
The edges of both plastic and metal scales must not deviate from a straight line by more than 0.5 mm at any point. Similarly, their plane surfaces must not vary from a flat plane by more than 0.5 mm.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15243 : 2002 is the national Indian Standard specification governing rigid velocity scale sets used for determining wind speed from plotted pilot balloon ascent hodographs in meteorological operations. Finalized by the Meteorological Instruments Sectional Committee (BP 21), it covers both three-scale sets and single flat plastic square scales with four graduated edges. The standard standardises exact physical distances for graduation intervals (from 1 m/s to 5 m/s) across different scale factors (1 cm = 1 km, 2 cm = 1 km, and 4 cm = 1 km), defines strict line length hierarchies for readability, and mandates tight tolerances on edge straightness and surface flatness (holding limits of 0.5 mm) for both plastic and metal scale variants.
